question: For a given real number $\alpha>0$, define $a_n=(1^\alpha+2^\alpha+\cdots+n^\alpha)^n$ and $b_n=n^n(n!)^\alpha$, for $n=1,2,\ldots$. Then

options.B: there exists an integer $n>1$ such that $a_n<b_n$
options.D: there exist integers $n$ and $m$ both larger than one such that $a_n>b_n$ and $a_m<b_m$

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10+2 Level — Sixteenth Edition
